sidcup.region: Sidcup and the London Borough of Bexley
sidcup.snapshot: Sidcup sits in the London Borough of Bexley, one of the better-served corners of south-east London for full fibre, and the network and cabling trade here runs on two routes. Build contractors and structured-cabling firms put crews on the street and order on trade accounts, while ex-BT sole traders and one-van broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account. We run both side by side.
sidcup.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Bexley and south-east London
s1loc: Sidcup sits in a busy patch of the full-fibre build across the London Borough of Bexley, which Openreach has named among its best-covered London boroughs for FTTP. Openreach delivery partners are pushing fibre through Sidcup, Foots Cray, North Cray and out toward Bexley village and Welling, Virgin Media O2 holds long-standing cable across the area, and alt-nets including Community Fibre and Hyperoptic reach parts of the borough. The result is a steady stream of civils gangs, jointing teams and provisioning engineers working the streets, footways and cabinets around the town and its neighbouring districts day to day.

Alongside the residential rollout sits a solid commercial scene. Sidcup has the Sidcup high street and station district, the Ruxley Corner and Blackfen trading areas, and large employers and offices that all need structured cabling, Cat6 and fibre backbones and CCTV. Add the schools, the local NHS sites and the warehouse and trade units toward Foots Cray, and there is steady work for cabling firms and CCTV installers wiring offices and multi-site premises. It is a mix of national contractors on the build and a long tail of independent engineers serving homes and businesses across Bexley.
